issues.title: Spike: measure manga chapter availability on real Prowlarr indexers
issues.body:
## Goal
Find out how often single chapters versus volumes are available on the indexers users actually run, before chapter monitoring is built around it.

## Scope
- Search 15 to 20 series (mix of ongoing, finished, manhwa, webtoon) through a real Prowlarr
- Record hits per series: chapters, volumes, packs, by indexer and category
- Save every release name found into `backend/tests/fixtures/releases/raw/` for the parser corpus

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Short written summary in `docs/spikes/chapter-availability.md`
- [ ] Raw release names committed (no URLs, no keys)
- [ ] Recommendation for the default monitor mode and fallback delay

## Refs
- CONTEXT/PRODUCT.md (Risks 1)

issues.title: Contribution policy: DCO or CLA
issues.body:
## Goal
Decide how outside contributions are accepted before the first one arrives.

## Scope
- Decide between a DCO (contributors certify they may submit the code) and a CLA (contributors also grant rights that allow relicensing)
- Note: a DCO alone does not let the maintainer dual-license contributed code. Keeping dual licensing open needs a CLA or accepting no outside code until one exists
- CONTRIBUTING.md with the chosen policy
- Enforcement: DCO sign-off check or a CLA bot on pull requests

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Decision recorded in PRODUCT.md (Business model) and an ADR
- [ ] CONTRIBUTING.md committed
- [ ] A PR without sign-off or signed CLA fails the check

## Refs
- CONTEXT/PRODUCT.md (Business model)

issues.title: API error responses and request IDs
issues.body:
## Goal
Every API error has the same shape and can be traced to a log line without leaking details.

## Scope
- Middleware assigns a request ID to every request and returns it in an `X-Request-ID` header
- Exception handlers return `{ code, message, request_id }`: a stable error code, a generic message, the request ID
- Error codes defined in one module; domain errors from `core/errors.py` map to codes and status codes
- Full details (exception, stack) logged with the request ID through the redaction filter
- Error schema documented in OpenAPI so the generated client knows it

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Unexpected exception returns 500 with the generic shape and no stack trace (tested)
- [ ] Validation error returns 400 with code and request ID (tested)
- [ ] Log line for the error carries the same request ID (tested)

## Refs
- CONTEXT/architecture-context.md (Error handling and logging)
- CONTEXT/code-standards.md (API)

issues.title: HTTP client factory with per-provider rate limits and response cache
issues.body:
## Goal
One place that creates outbound HTTP clients so limits and caching are never skipped.

## Scope
- `core/http.py` returns an httpx AsyncClient per adapter
- Per-adapter rate limiter (requests per interval)
- Response cache table keyed by request, TTL per adapter
- 429 raises `RateLimited` with retry-after

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Two concurrent calls respect the limiter (tested)
- [ ] Cached response is returned without a network call (tested with cassette)
- [ ] No other module creates an AsyncClient

## Refs
- CONTEXT/architecture-context.md (Rate limits and caching)

issues.title: Quality profiles and the Decision engine
issues.body:
## Goal
Accept or reject every Parsed release with a score and readable reasons.

## Scope
- Profile: digital vs scan, file format order, languages, preferred groups, cutoff
- Decision includes score, Confidence and reasons
- Pack handling (skip volumes already on disk)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every rejection has a reason string
- [ ] Tests cover at least these cases:
  - Full digital volume in the profile's language: accepted, scored above a scan of the same volume
  - Chapter range that matches Wanted chapters: accepted
  - Pack with some volumes already on disk: accepted, with a reason noting which volumes are skipped
  - Release in a language not in the profile: rejected, "Language not in profile"
  - Spin-off whose title contains the series title: rejected as a different series
  - Release for an Edition that isn't monitored (for example an omnibus): rejected, "Edition not monitored"

## Refs
- CONTEXT/CONTEXT.md (Decision, Confidence, Quality profile)

issues.title: FallbackToChapterSource command and Suwayomi import
issues.body:
## Goal
Fill chapter gaps after Prowlarr had its chance.

## Scope
- Scheduled; picks wanted Chapters older than the Fallback delay with no grab in progress
- Enqueues download in Suwayomi; never for Volumes or Upgrades
- Import from the shared Suwayomi download folder (CBZ on)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Chapter with a pending Prowlarr grab is skipped (tested)
- [ ] Chapter missing from the source list stays Wanted
- [ ] Imported chapters follow the normal pipeline

## Refs
- docs/adr/0006

issues.title: Series detail page
issues.body:
## Goal
The main screen: editions, volumes, chapters and where data came from.

## Scope
- Edition switcher; volume list for the selected Edition
- Expandable volume rows with a chapter grid
- Mapping provenance with edit and lock
- Synopsis with original and translation toggle
- Unstyled headless primitives; no design system yet

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each volume row shows: number, title for the selected Edition, chapter range and count, mapping provenance, status (downloaded, partial with x of y, wanted, unmonitored)
- [ ] Switching Edition changes volume titles and splits; Chapters on disk stay the same
- [ ] Expanded row shows each chapter as on disk or wanted, and the mapping's provenance detail
- [ ] Synopsis shows a machine-translated label with the model name, and switches to the original text
- [ ] Lock and edit call the API and survive a metadata refresh
- [ ] Status is shown with text, not color alone

## Refs
- CONTEXT/CONTEXT.md (Edition, Mapping, Provenance, Locked, Translation)
- docs/adr/0003
